newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sanofi sees alliances, no merger - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sanofi sees alliances, no merger - paper.

text.p: Sanofi, the health and beauty products group majority-owned by Elf Aquitaine is looking for alliances to spread the risks of developing new products, chairman Jean-Francois Dehecq told Le Monde.
But he excluded a wide-ranging merger, such as an often-rumoured link with Rhone-Poulenc drug unit Rhone-Poulenc Rorer.
"We want to strengthen our position market by market. Meanwhile it is not excluded that we would strike alliances if there is an opportunity," Dehecq said in an interview.
"We have a remarkable financial health with 20 billion francs in shareholders' funds and hardly any debts," he said.
"The race for size is justified when you do not have products and you need to improve results. That is not our case," he said.
Asked to comment on a possible link between Sanofi and Rorer, he said "Today, all of us are convinced that such a merger would bring many more disadvantages than advantages," he added.
